appraisal_events.evidence: "Ah ! princesse, vous savez bien qu'ils ne se tiendraient pas de joie…"; the narrator adds that her demurral was, in part, because she was in fact "une des plus grandes dames de France."
appraisal_events.explanation: The général's admiring remark, together with the narrator's explicit gloss confirming her real social pre-eminence, elevates the princesse/duchesse even as she performs playful modesty and displays her celebrated wit in refusing the compliment.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator directly confirms she is one of the greatest ladies of France, and her exclusive refusal to call on people she does not know reinforces rather than undercuts her elite standing.
Her extended, witty rejoinder about Vercingétorix and Spartacus displays conversational command and discernment, reinforcing her rhetorical authority in the exchange.

ambiguities: "le général" is never named in the passage itself; his identification with the reference sheet's général de Froberville relies on chapter-level context (the Sainte-Euverte soirée) rather than an in-passage proper name.
